data.narrative:
Critical Energy, a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Spencer Jackson, has raised $22M to date. The valuation landscape includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with aligned valuation tiers to support a reliable median-based approach.

The Stage-Progression method is the primary applicable triangulation technique here. Using total capital raised of $22M as a Seed-stage proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding round yields an implied valuation of $55M. This method reflects observed progression dynamics in early-stage venture outcomes but carries inherent stage-specific assumptions.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $47M to $63M, centered on $55M. The median estimate derives from a single methodological source, which substantially limits confidence. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer comps at the same stage and valuation tier; the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier to Critical Energy's specific risk and market position; and unobserved company fundamentals including burn rate, runway, and product-market progress. Additional diligence on unit economics and competitive positioning would be necessary to refine this estimate materially.
